solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gentle guy who nicks whisky finally? It doesn't get to print

parts.note: gentle means soft
a policeman nicks (arrests) people, so he is a cop

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word whisky

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered man pinches whisky, a cheeky question tacked on before a remark about printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicks' is British slang for arrests, so the guy who nicks is a policeman. The definition is a cryptic hint at an electronic document that never reaches paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic version of a document, viewed on screen, is never put on paper.

clue.text: Dwarf mole finding shelter inside

indicators.note: inside means the shelter goes within the mole

parts.note: a mole is an undercover agent, a spy
lee is a sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: A small mole burrowing into a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The dwarf is one of the seven in Snow White; 'mole' is a spy, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Snow White's seven little companions in the Disney film is named for drowsiness.

clue.text: Marked agent gets round litigation

indicators.note: gets round means the agent surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a fed is an FBI agent
law covers litigation, going to court

explanation.surface: A tainted secret agent evades a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marked is blemished or defective, carrying a fault.

clue.text: A herb from Switzerland I have

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a herb brought back from Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A small onion-family plant whose leaves are used in cooking as a herb.

clue.text: Looking closely at making a noble?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as the act of turning someone into a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: Studying how an aristocrat is created.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented sense: ennobling someone, punned as conferring the rank of peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Squinting carefully at something is the plain sense; the punning one is creating a lord.

clue.text: Harpy is grabbing good food for Jock

indicators.note: grabbing means the outer pieces hold the next piece between them

parts.note: a harpy is a shrewish woman, a hag

explanation.surface: A greedy harridan snatches the tasty food meant for a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman, so food for Jock is a Scottish dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis, the minced offal pudding, is Scotland's national dish.

clue.text: This is next to a hypotenuse!

parts.note: the hypotenuse is the longest side of a right-angled triangle

explanation.surface: An exclamation pointing at the right-angled triangle's longest edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is' is a link: a hypotenuse is a long side.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside, at the side of, adjacent to something.

clue.text: Place for rushing or riding excitedly

indicators.note: excitedly says the letters of or riding are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A spot for hurrying or galloping about in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rushing' is the American football term for running with the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: An American football field is nicknamed for its striped lines, where players run the ball.

clue.text: Office equipment is quiet and more revolutionary

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
red stands for revolutionary, so redder is more so

explanation.surface: A piece of office kit is silent and more radical.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine for cutting unwanted papers into strips is common workplace kit.

clue.text: One trying former African leader and ruler

parts.note: ex- means former
Idi Amin led Uganda in the 1970s
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone putting a former African dictator and a monarch on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' suggests a court, but here it means testing candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tests candidates in an exam is trying them, putting their knowledge to the test.

clue.text: PC that is right for office equipment

parts.note: PC is a police constable, a cop
i.e. is the abbreviation of 'id est', that is

explanation.surface: A personal computer is the correct choice of kit for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a computer, but here it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopying machine is standard workplace kit.

clue.text: Alternatively long-armed giant

indicators.note: alternatively here means taking every other letter of long-armed

explanation.surface: Either way, a monster with long arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of LONG-ARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating monster in folklore is a kind of giant.

clue.text: Immediately before parking and returning

parts.note: P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking
receding means drawing back, going back

explanation.surface: Just before parking a car, the driver comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coming directly ahead of another in order or time goes just in front of it.

clue.text: Putting name in where you write could be a bore

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is put inside another

parts.note: in a crossword you write your answers in the grid

explanation.surface: Filling in a name on a form could be tedious work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' is a link; 'where you write' is the crossword grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious, wearying work, a slog, is called a dull chore or tiresome drudgery.

clue.text: Succeed with good fan

parts.note: to succeed is to win

explanation.surface: Coming out on top along with a good supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like a supporter, but Chambers gives it as a poetic word for a bird's limb used in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an old poetic term for a feathered limb that beats the air.

clue.text: Harsh line accepted by popular union

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: accepted by means the line goes inside the union

parts.note: cement is a bond or union

explanation.surface: A popular trade union takes a hard line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' is a bond, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement weather is severe, stormy and rough.

clue.text: Incident is found in lyric poem

indicators.note: found in means the first piece is sitting inside the second

parts.note: an epode is a kind of lyric poem

explanation.surface: An event is recorded in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single event or occurrence in a series.

clue.text: Vicious insult about King in command

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark
a. is an abbreviation for about, used with dates
R is Rex, king
i/c means in charge or in command

explanation.surface: A cruel jibe directed at the monarch in power.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage, brutal and uncivilised behaviour is described as vicious.

clue.text: US commando on street is an unknown bloke

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the commando piece sits below the street piece

parts.note: the US Army Rangers are an elite commando unit

explanation.surface: A soldier on the street is a man nobody recognises.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone you have never met is a man unfamiliar to you.

clue.text: Eg, a recital moved

indicators.note: moved means the letters of recital are shifted round into a new order

explanation.surface: For example, a recital that moved its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Eg, a': the word 'a' is an example of the grammatical part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls 'a' the indefinite one of this part of speech, alongside 'the'.

clue.text: Some see a cheat in every individual

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people see a cheat in everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied to every individual one separately; 'in every individual' works as an adverbial sense.

clue.text: Writer finding time for himself, say

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: An author makes time for his own work.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe plus T describes Poe himself: 'say' marks him as one example of the kind of writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe wrote verse such as The Raven, so he himself is an example of a verse writer.

clue.text: Helping with the introduction of California's humour

indicators.note: introduction here means something is put into the first piece

parts.note: a plate is a plateful, a helping of food
CA is the abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Assisting with the arrival of California's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humour' is a verb here: to go along with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour someone is to soothe or pacify them by indulging them.

clue.text: An island sheep upset a place to lie up

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the whole string upside down

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep on an island gets knocked over somewhere it can rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses the whole run AN I RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats are moored, or laid up, in a harbour for yachts.

clue.text: Welsh tranforming green energy

indicators.note: transforming (misspelt in the clue) says the letters of green change into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Wales converting to green energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' is the verb meaning to break a promise, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh on a deal is to go back on a promise.

clue.text: Support British expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Backing a skilled Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a prop or strut that holds something up.

clue.text: Wife, say, with elegance with whom you studied

parts.note: class means style, elegance
a wife is an example of a mate, a partner

explanation.surface: Your stylish wife was once the person you studied alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow pupil in the same school form is someone you learned with.

clue.text: Most unfavourably comment on small behind

parts.note: late means behind time

explanation.surface: Making a harsh remark about a little backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a backside but means overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: To criticise harshly, as in a hostile review.

clue.text: Covering German's informal game

parts.note: a rug is a covering for a floor
GER is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A German's covering for a casual game.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition says 'informal' because this is the slang name for rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial British name for rugby football, the game.

clue.text: Supplement could be amazing drug

indicators.note: could be says the letters of amazing might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dietary supplement might turn out to be a wonder drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplement' suggests vitamins, but here it is the colour section of a newspaper; E is slang for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's colour supplement is a glossy periodical inserted in the weekend edition.

clue.text: Copper to think highly of clergyman

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rate someone is to think highly of them

explanation.surface: A police officer admires a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant parish priest in the Church of England is this kind of churchman.

clue.text: Calm about a dead romantic song

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: serene means calm

explanation.surface: A tranquil love song about someone who has died.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover traditionally sings this evening tune beneath a beloved's window.
